patch_description:
The previous implementation failed validation because it could lose row identity, alter column structure through merge operations, write grouped rows using completion-order indices, and return an empty `column_orderings` list despite permuting data. It also relied on attribute access for column names, which is invalid for many legitimate DataFrame column labels.

This replacement preserves every row, value, shape, index, and column label. It computes serialization-only string representations without changing stored values, creates valid per-row column orderings, honors merge groups as contiguous ordering blocks and dependency constraints as precedence constraints, and selects between bounded candidate orderings using the actual sorted-string LCP Trie objective.
